system.name: DChannel
system.one_liner: a system that accelerates mobile applications by steering traffic across parallel high-bandwidth and low-latency cellular channels

components.name: Client app
components.role: mobile application generating traffic to be accelerated

components.name: DChannel client
components.role: client-side agent that steers outgoing traffic across HBC and LLC and reorders incoming traffic

components.name: Packet steerer
components.role: steers application traffic to the LLC and HBC channels

components.name: Reordering buffer
components.role: reorders packets coming from the LLC before passing them to the app

components.name: DChannel proxy
components.role: proxy-side agent in the packet core gateway performing the symmetric steering and reordering functions

components.name: Reordering buffer
components.role: reorders packets coming from the LLC on the proxy side

components.name: Packet steerer
components.role: steers traffic headed toward the client between LLC and HBC

components.name: App server
components.role: remote server the mobile app communicates with over the Internet

content.key_idea: Mirrored client and proxy agents each split traffic across a high-bandwidth channel and a low-latency channel, then reorder what arrives over the low-latency channel before delivering it.
content.reading_order: Left to right across the network path (User equipment to Internet), matching the symmetric Packet steerer / Reordering buffer pair on the client against the same pair on the proxy.

summary: Figure 1 gives DChannel's end-to-end overview across five network zones: User equipment, Base station, Core network, Packet core gateway, and Internet. On the client, a Client app sends traffic through a virtual interface into the DChannel client, whose Packet steerer splits traffic across two parallel paths, HBC (high-bandwidth) and LLC (low-latency), while its Reordering buffer reassembles packets arriving over LLC. The Packet core gateway hosts a symmetric DChannel proxy with its own Packet steerer and Reordering buffer, performing the mirrored function for traffic headed toward the client and toward the Internet, where it exchanges ordinary IP packets with an App server. The figure uses a swimlane layout to show the network path and colored dashed arrows to distinguish the HBC and LLC channels between the two mirrored DChannel agents.
